LITHOLOGY_MODIFIER: Quartzose (boulder) conglomerate. In the southern part of the workings it is a coarse conglomerate composed of boulders up to 0.6m in diameter of rounded to sub-angular quartz and quartzite in a kaolinitic gritty matrix. Northwards, the unit becomes thinner and finer grained consisting of 12-14m of sandstone with scattered boulders and pebbles .

The zone consists of sheared and brecciated greywacke-tillite and fine dark quartzite with kaolinitic material and ferruginous gossan,  to brecciated siliceous zones with quartz and ferruginous ironstone gossan at suface. At depth the zone is composed of quartz-chlorite-sericite fragments surrounded by pyrite and minor chalcopyrite, passing into meta-siltstones strongly fractured with pyrite and minor chalcopyrite, with fracturing decreasing away from the  shear zone.
